identity.resolvedIdentity: The former Hakadal ironworks and coherent works, waterpower, worker, school and estate environment, physically anchored in the named surviving industrial building.
identity.identityProblem: Most direct production structures have disappeared. A surviving named building can anchor the wider institution and landscape, but must not be presented as the exact location of every historic production phase.
identity.splitReason: The ironworks, water systems, main building, iron store, worker housing, school and estate landscape form one coherent historic institutional environment.

documented operating period and resource system
documentation of surviving and disappeared components
named physical geometry on the works site

evidence.finding: SNL identifies Hakadal Verk as a former ironworks established around 1550 and closed in 1869 and describes surviving dams, falls, industrial buildings, the main building, worker housing, school and crofter communities.
evidence.reason: Confirms the historical identity and wider works environment; OSM supplies the applied geometry.

evidence.finding: The local history documents production, ore from Grua, royal privileges, ownership, closure in 1869 and the disappearance of most direct iron-production traces apart from the main building and old iron store.
evidence.reason: Explains why the surviving building is an area anchor rather than an exact furnace or smelting-site coordinate.

evidence.finding: Way 249239760 is named Hakadal verk and tagged historic=works and building=industrial with national building reference 151094600. Its nine-node polygon has calculated centroid 60.122400847631, 10.824335391711.
evidence.reason: Provides a stable named same-site physical object and reproducible geometry for the area anchor.

evidence.finding: Nominatim resolves way 249239760 as Hakadal verk, type works and category historic, with point 60.1224095, 10.8243370 approximately one metre from the calculated centroid.
evidence.reason: Cross-checks object identity and centroid calculation.

evidence.finding: SNL describes an early Hakadal rennverk phase in 1541–1545 and later attempts before an ironworks was founded on the same site.
evidence.reason: Prevents the surviving building from being misrepresented as every historical production structure.

evidence.finding: The previous coordinate 60.12083, 10.82278 lies approximately 194.8 metres south-west of the named works-building centroid and lacked a source contract.
